The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24541.name: Scourge Precision Cruise Missile

25715.description: A launcher intended for use on cruiser-class spacecraft. While assault launchers do not possess the sheer damage-dealing capability of regular heavy missile launchers, their blend of speed and attack power lends them application across a good range of tactical situations.
25715.name: Heavy Assault Missile Launcher II

16487.name: Large Inductive Compact Remote Capacitor Transmitter

expected.note: Hand-derived 2026-10-09 against real killmail 139013625 (Leshak, 1x Veles Supratidal Entropic Disintegrator / Meson Exotic Plasma L, 1x Entropic Radiation Sink I, 4x Wasp II deployable [100/100 bandwidth] + 5x Warrior II in bay but NOT deployable [0 bandwidth room left], Armor Maintenance Bot/Hornet EC-300 non-combat). Verifies the new SHIP_ROLE_BONUS[47271] = [['precursor','damage',25],['precursor','rof',25]] entry (bug #26 follow-up / Leshak fix): turret DPS = 616(dmg sum)*1.04(wpn mult)*dmgSkillMult(1.15*1.25*1.09*1.25=1.95859375)*spoolup(3.125) / (8.0*0.80*0.90*0.96*0.75=4.1472s) = 945.48; + drone DPS 54/drone*4 deployable Wasp II = 216 (Warrior II's 5 units get 0 deployable, bandwidth already full) => dpsFixed ~= 1161. Verified the revert-and-diff regression guard: temporarily deleting the new SHIP_ROLE_BONUS[47271] entry (dmgSkillMult drops to 1.15*1.25*1.09=1.565875, rofSkillMult's hull factor back to 1 so cycle=8*0.80*0.90*0.96=5.5296s) drops this fit's actual computed dpsFixed from 1161 to 783 (turret-only DPS 945.48->567, a 1.667x ratio matching the predicted 1.25x(damage)*1.333x(rof) undercount) -- confirms this fit actually catches the fix. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (comprehensive skill audit, P1-B): drone DPS multiplier corrected -- the RoF reduction previously applied (-20%, attributed to '[Race] Drone Specialization') was fictional, no drone RoF skill exists at all; that skill is actually a +10%@V DAMAGE bonus gated to T2 drones (reqSkill-detected), and a separate, previously entirely unmodeled weapon-size-class damage skill (+25%@V, Light/Medium/Heavy Drone Operation or Sentry Drone Interfacing, always applies) was added. 267.description: An ultra-heavy piercing missile. While it is a slow projectile, its sheer damage potential is simply staggering.
267.name: Scourge Torpedo

527.description: Reduces the maximum speed of a ship by employing micro energy streams which effectively entangle the target temporarily, thereby slowing it down.
527.name: Stasis Webifier II

2048.description:
Utilizes a combination of containment field emitters and redundancy systems to mitigate the impact of critical system damage. 

Grants a bonus to resistance for shield, armor and hull.

Only one Damage Control can be fit at a given time.
2048.name: Damage Control II

2404.description: Favored by many for its average capacity and firing rate. Useful in both fast attack raids and longer battles.
2404.name: Light Missile Launcher II

2410.description: Designed for long engagements between medium sized ships. Slow firing rate, but makes up for it with a large missile capacity.
2410.name: Heavy Missile Launcher II

2420.description: A massive launcher designed for extended bombardments of hard targets like battleships and stations. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
2420.name: Torpedo Launcher II

2629.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
2629.name: Scourge Fury Heavy Missile

3244.description: Disrupts the target ship's navigation computer which prevents it from warping.
3244.name: Warp Disruptor II

10631.description: A tiny launcher that can carry a very limited supply of rockets. Not really intended as a primary weapon but rather as a cheap supplementary weapon system.
10631.name: Rocket Launcher II

11578.description:
A very specialized piece of technology, the covert ops cloak is designed for use in tandem with specific covert ops vessels. Although it could theoretically work on other ships, its spatial distortion field is so unstable that trying to compensate for its fluctuations will overwhelm non-specialized computing hardware. 

Note: This particular module is advanced enough that it allows a ship to warp while cloaked. However, fitting two or more cloaking devices to a ship negates their use, as unsynchronized light deflection causes interference.
11578.name: Covert Ops Cloaking Device II

12267.description: Neutralizes a portion of the energy in the target ship's capacitor.
12267.name: Medium Energy Neutralizer II

19739.description: A battleship mounted launcher used for long range standoffs with other battleships, but less suitable for bombardment of deployed structures. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
19739.name: Cruise Missile Launcher II

20307.description: A kinetic warhead designed for use with heavy assault launchers. Heavy assault missiles can be fired at a greater rate than heavy missiles, at the expense of effective range.
20307.name: Scourge Heavy Assault Missile

22291.description:
A computer system designed for monitoring and guiding missiles in flight, thus allowing for superior effectiveness and lethality. 

Penalty: Using more than one type of this module or similar modules that affect the same attribute on the ship will be penalized.
22291.name: Ballistic Control System II

24471.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

This modified version of the Scourge rocket packs a considerably stronger punch, but as a result is heavier and slower. This makes it very effective against larger targets, but markedly less effective against smaller and more agile targets.
24471.name: Scourge Rage Rocket

24477.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

A modified version of the Scourge rocket. It can reach higher velocity than the Scourge rocket at the expense of warhead size.
24477.name: Scourge Javelin Rocket

24490.description:
An EMP warhead designed for use with heavy assault launchers. Heavy assault missiles can be fired at a greater rate than heavy missiles, at the expense of effective range.

This modified version of the Mjolnir Heavy Assault Missile packs a considerably stronger punch, but as a result is heavier and slower. This makes it very effective against larger targets, but markedly less effective against smaller and more agile targets.
24490.name: Mjolnir Rage Heavy Assault Missile

28668.description:
A thick, heavy liquid, typically stored in tanks or container systems intended for liquids. It is composed of billions of nanites that can be programmed to repair damaged ship modules on the fly. The paste is simply applied to the damaged area, and the nanites meld into an exact copy of the damaged area, thus effecting repairs upon the module. This is a one-time process, as the nanites use themselves up along with the trace elements mixed into their carrier fluid.

The Repair Paste is generally only used for emergency on-site repairs. It is then recommended to have the damaged components looked at by a certified technician at first opportunity.
28668.name: Nanite Repair Paste

28756.description: Launcher for Core Scanner Probes and Combat Scanner Probes. Core Scanner Probes are used to scan down Cosmic Signatures in space. Combat Scanner Probes are used to scan down Cosmic Signatures, starships, structures and drones. Note: Only one scan probe launcher can be fitted per ship. 10% bonus to strength of scan probes.
28756.name: Sisters Expanded Probe Launcher

29990.description: For many Minmatar, the high mountains of Matar hold wonders unknown to the rest of New Eden: hidden glens, beautiful creatures, buried customs. Not surprisingly, the Krusual tribe lay claim to these mountains, their home for generations and base to their machinations. Krusual elders whisper ancient tales among their huddled tribes, describing the glory of heroes past and enigmatic prophecies of old. On the darkest day, at the most hopeless moments, an elder may speak of Loki, in reverent tones and excited hushes. In the ancient tongue, the Loki are the crux of Krusual thought. There is no direct translation for this word; in fact, Loki translates differently among the elders. It can mean “hidden wonder” or “secret passage”, “changing mask” or “unseen dagger”. Regardless of its context, Loki has one meaning common to all its tales across all the elders: “hope”.
29990.name: Loki

30486.description: A scanner probe used for scanning down Cosmic Signatures, starships, structures and drones. Can be launched from Expanded Probe Launchers.
30486.name: Sisters Combat Scanner Probe

31754.description: This ship modification is designed to increase the thermal resistance of ship shields at the expense of increased signature radius. Penalty: Using more than one type of this module or similar modules that affect the same attribute on the ship will be penalized. The drawbacks of fitting this rig may be reduced by training the Shield Rigging skill.
31754.name: Medium Thermal Shield Reinforcer I

31796.description: This ship modification is designed to increase shield capacity at the expense of increased signature radius. The drawbacks of fitting this rig may be reduced by training the Shield Rigging skill.
31796.name: Medium Core Defense Field Extender II

31932.description: Increases the maximum strength of the shield.
31932.name: Republic Fleet Large Shield Extender

35659.description:
Massive boost to speed for a very short time. The thrust that boosts the ship, and the corresponding maximum velocity bonus, are limited by the mass of the ship that uses this module. The sheer amount of energy needed to power this system means that it must permanently reserve a fraction of the capacitor output just to maintain the integrity of its warp containment field, and when activated it substantially increases the ship's EM footprint.

Penalty: Max capacitor reduced.

Note: Usually fit on Cruisers and Battlecruisers.
35659.name: 50MN Y-T8 Compact Microwarpdrive

45595.description:
From the moment Strategic Cruisers became a reality, there were whispers amongst the scientific community about the potential for advances in cloaking technology. They remained that alone for the longest time, with few involved in the reverse engineering process willing to share any news of their discoveries. Everyone knew that, should the technology ever become a reality, the capabilities of the new Strategic Cruisers would change overnight.    

The Loki's Covert Reconfiguration designs arose out of a collective will to respond to what was thought to be Amarrian aggression deep inside their home regions. Unlike many scientific and technological breakthroughs, it was not the Sebiestor tribe alone who ushered in the paradigm shift to covert-capable Strategic Cruisers. It was only through consultation and collaboration with many other tribes and sub-factions that something substantial began to take shape. 

The Krusual and Thukker are said to have played the most important roles, however, in realizing the final design; the Thukker by providing the cloaking technology, and the Krusual by convincing them to do so. How they achieved this, or what they may have promised remains a secret; the two tribes are notorious for having many, and keeping them all.
45595.name: Loki Defensive - Covert Reconfiguration

45608.description: Adaptation and innovation go hand-in-hand, and this subsystem is a prime example of both ideas. While researching Sleeper drone weapon systems, a group of Minmatar engineers discovered that Sleeper launcher hardpoint design allowed for a vast increase to the rate of fire without increasing powergrid requirements. The resulting subsystem allows the Loki to achieve some of the most aggressive missile configurations seen on any cruiser.
45608.name: Loki Offensive - Launcher Efficiency Configuration

45620.description: Constructed from hard yet lightweight fullerene polymers, these intercalated fibers boost the speed and agility of a starship without compromising its structural resilience. Even though basic nanofibers have existed for hundreds of years, the integration of various Sleeper-based salvage and other polymers takes the technology to a completely new level of modularity. This has allowed the same centuries-old technology to be ported over to the new Tech III paradigm.
45620.name: Loki Propulsion - Intercalated Nanofibers

45633.description: Even millennia old, the technology employed by Sleeper drones is far from lacking. This is particularly true in the field of interdiction technology, where their capabilities often exceed contemporary systems. Consequently, this aspect of their fearsome arsenal has been the focus of much study and in some rare cases, the starting point for scientific breakthroughs. Minmatar researchers studied the long-range webification systems of the Sleeper drones from the moment they were discovered, quickly reverse engineering a subsystem for their Loki that could replicate the Sleeper's own offensive modules. The end result is a noticeable amplification of a stasis webifier's effective range.
45633.name: Loki Core - Immobility Drivers

45998.description: +3% turret damage, +3% missile damage, 3% vorton projector damage. Duration 30 minutes. A novel and powerful addition to the range of neural boosters available to capsuleers, the Agency's ‘Pyrolancea’ compounds introduce a temporary but highly adaptive neural lace into the user’s synaptic structures. This 'Pyrolancea' lace enhances neural centers involved in calibration of munitions payloads and weapons energy profiles on the fly during high-intensity combat. The increase in the processing available to the capsuleer means that payload calibration solutions can be tailored more finely and results in improved damage yields against any given target. Compounds with the Agency identifier are being seeded into target locations identified by the mysterious network ahead of sponsored operations. Entities occupying the target sites often collect the Agency's support drops themselves even if they realize what they must portend. The Agency’s novel method of supporting capsuleer operations is thought to be as much an experiment as it is an incentive for freelance pilots to take up the public contracts.
45998.name: Agency 'Pyrolancea' DB3 Dose I

45999.description: +5% turret damage, +5% missile damage, 5% vorton projector damage. Duration 30 minutes. A novel and powerful addition to the range of neural boosters available to capsuleers, the Agency's ‘Pyrolancea’ compounds introduce a temporary but highly adaptive neural lace into the user’s synaptic structures. This 'Pyrolancea' lace enhances neural centers involved in calibration of munitions payloads and weapons energy profiles on the fly during high-intensity combat. The increase in the processing available to the capsuleer means that payload calibration solutions can be tailored more finely and results in improved damage yields against any given target. Compounds with the Agency identifier are being seeded into target locations identified by the mysterious network ahead of sponsored operations. Entities occupying the target sites often collect the Agency's support drops themselves even if they realize what they must portend. The Agency’s novel method of supporting capsuleer operations is thought to be as much an experiment as it is an incentive for freelance pilots to take up the public contracts.
45999.name: Agency 'Pyrolancea' DB5 Dose II

expected.note: Real pyfa cross-check (2026-10-10) against killmail 138935092 -- a Loki (T3 Strategic Cruiser), 5x Heavy Assault Missile Launcher II/Mjolnir Rage Heavy Assault Missile, 3x Ballistic Control System II, Republic Fleet Large Shield Extender + 50MN Y-T8 Compact MWD + 2x Stasis Webifier II + Warp Disruptor II, Damage Control II, 2x Medium Core Defense Field Extender II + Medium Thermal Shield Reinforcer I rigs, standard Loki subsystems (Immobility Drivers/Covert Reconfiguration/Launcher Efficiency Configuration/Intercalated Nanofibers). pyfa reported DPS 801 (exact match to the tool own dpsFixed) and EHP 33.9k/shield 21.4k/armor 6.29k/hull 6.22k -- all consistent with the tool own computed exact values (33896/21386/6291/6219), which round to those same pyfa figures. unmatchedWeaponCount=1 is the Sisters Expanded Probe Launcher, a known cosmetic-only miscount (KNOWN OPEN ITEM #2 in [[dscan-tool]] -- Probe Launchers misclassified as unresolved weapons, no false DPS). Scaffolded via scaffold_golden_fit.mjs (Phase 5) from a real, live-fetched killmail (not hand-typed) -- the first golden fit built this way, and the first closed-loop proof the scaffolder pipeline end-to-end (live fetch -> assembly -> provisional compute -> real pyfa confirmation) actually works. Loki sensor-strength re-investigation ADDED 2026-10-11: sensorStrengthValue now asserts this fit genuinely has NO sensor-strength bonus -- the previously-flagged open gap (pyfa figure 20.4 vs. this tool 17, Ladar) is RESOLVED as a different-subsystem mismatch, not a bug. Confirmed live via ESI across all 3 real variants of each of the Loki Core/Defensive/Offensive/Propulsion Subsystem slots (12 types total) that only one -- Loki Core - Dissolution Sequencer (type 45631), NOT Immobility Drivers (type 45633, what THIS killmail actually fitted) -- carries any effect touching sensor-strength attributes 208-211 (a PostPercent bonus to Ladar/209 via container attribute 1446, itself scaled by Minmatar Core Systems skill -- same required-skill-scales-a-container-attribute architecture as the earlier Tengu/Proteus EWAR bug). 17 base x 1.20 (Dissolution Sequencer @ Minmatar Core Systems V, by this codebase established per-level pattern) = 20.4, an exact match to the pasted pyfa figure -- strong evidence pyfa was showing a Loki fitted WITH Dissolution Sequencer, not this fit's actual Immobility Drivers. See dscan-tool-architecture.md and the SCAN_STRENGTH_ATTRS comment in dscan-tool.html. UPDATE (independent review finding #18, 2026-10-11): KNOWN OPEN ITEM #2 (Probe Launcher miscounted as an unresolved weapon) is now FIXED -- weaponCategoryFromGroup() returning null for the Sisters Expanded Probe Launcher (Scan Probe Launcher group) is now checked BEFORE incrementing variableWeaponCount/pushing to unresolvedWeapons, not after, so it is excluded from this accounting entirely instead of permanently stuck as unresolved. variableWeaponCount 6->5 (the probe launcher no longer counted at all), unmatchedWeaponCount 1->0 (nothing left unresolved -- all 5 real HAM II launchers are confirmed via their loaded Mjolnir Rage charge, as before). UPDATE 2026-10-11 (backlog #1): speedCruising/alignTimeBase added -- this real killmail fit already has 45620 (Loki Propulsion - Intercalated Nanofibers) fitted, confirmed live via ESI to carry the exact same +5%/lvl maxVelocity / -5%/lvl agility magnitude as Legion's 45611 (Minmatar Propulsion Systems skill@V scaling 1450/1523 the same way Amarr's scales 1435/1512 for Legion -- see SUBSYSTEM_SPEED_AGILITY_BONUS's comment). Hand-derived: 185*1.25*1.25=289.06 (289); -ln(0.25)*(0.54*0.75*0.75)*13.8=5.81 (5.8) -- exact tool match, confirms the table applies correctly for a 2nd race via a real (not constructed) fit. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (backlog #16, NEGATIVE CONTROL): capacitorCapacity (1875) pinned -- this fit's Core subsystem (if any) is not one of the capacitor-bonus 'Reactor' ids, confirming SUBSYSTEM_CAPACITOR_CAPACITY_SELFADD_ATTR correctly contributes zero here. CORRECTED 2026-10-12: the 2026-10-11 re-investigation above reached the right final number (20.4) via the WRONG mechanism (misattributed to a different Loki Core subsystem, Dissolution Sequencer, that this kill never fitted) -- the real root cause, found via the owner real Svipul-fit bug report (KNOWN OPEN ITEM #1 in dscan-tool.md), is the universal Ladar Sensor Compensation skill (type 33001, ESI skill group 1213 "Targeting" -- the very group the original check claimed to have exhaustively ruled out), +20% at V, independent of subsystem entirely. Tool fixed to apply MAX_SENSOR_COMPENSATION_MULT=1.20 to every ship sensor-strength figure; this fit sensorStrengthValue expectation updated 17->20.4 to match the corrected formula (and the pyfa figure that was on file the whole time). See dscan-tool.html SCAN_STRENGTH_ATTRS comment for the full corrected mechanism writeup. UPDATE 2026-10-13 (speed/align completeness pass): Spaceship Command V (-2%/lvl agility, every ship, pyfa evasiveManeuveringAgilityBonusPostPercentAgilityShip on skill 3327) was never modeled -- every align time x0.90.  New values: alignTimeBase 5.2. UPDATE 2026-10-13 (v2026.10.13.11, capacitor batch): capacitorCapacity 1875 -> 1406: the fitted MWD's attr147 = 0.75 IS a real capacity penalty -- pyfa capacitorCapacityMultiply (effect 58) is on every MWD, applied unpenalized. The 2026-10-12 group gate excluded it as a 'collision'; capacity/recharge are now read via their real effects (58/51). Active drain 38.9 -> 29.2 (independent hand check 29.175: Propulsion Jamming x0.75 webs/scram, HSM x0.75 MWD, Capacitor Emission Systems x0.75 neut). UPDATE v2026.10.14.11 (EWAR from pyfa handlers, hand-tables P4; values from tools/independent_checks/compare_ewar.py): Stasis Webifier II range 10,000 x 2.25 = 22,500 m (Loki Core - Immobility Drivers, Effect4274, 25%/level; v.10's hand subsystem table had no Loki entry).

expected.note: EWAR capabilities card regression guard (F3, 2026-10-11), built from a real, live-ESI-fetched loss (zKillboard 139073592, hash dc40ad4503d86ee8f768695ef2078ccdd9561f0d) chosen specifically because it stacks 3 distinct EWAR module types across both tracked categories on one hull: Caldari Navy Warp Disruptor (tackle/scram, 26km, strength 1), Guidance Disruptor II (disrupt, 48km, missileVelocityBonusPct=-9/flightTimeBonusPct=-9), and 2x Tracking Disruptor II (disrupt, 48km each, opticalBonusPct=-17.19/falloffBonusPct=-17.19/trackingSpeedBonusPct=-17.19) -- 4 modules total, 3 distinct names, confirming both the shared-ESI-group-291 name-based split (Tracking vs. Guidance Disruptor) and the longest-range-first sort (both 48km disruptors ahead of the 26km scram). This fit also happens to carry zero turrets/launchers (all 5 high slots are cap warfare: 3x Small + 2x Medium Energy Neutralizer II), so dpsFixed/droneDps/HP below come entirely from the drone bay (5x Acolyte II + 3x Infiltrator II, Hornet EC-300 ECM drones excluded as non-combat) and the fitted Medium Ancillary Armor Repairer (296x Nanite Repair Paste charges) -- these are the tool's own sandbox-computed values (not independently pyfa-cross-checked, since this fit's purpose is EWAR coverage, not DPS methodology) and are pinned at a wide tolerance purely as a 'did anything else regress' guard, not a precision claim. UPDATED 2026-10-11 (EWAR effectiveness bonuses, F-item): ewarLongestRangeM/ewarTdRangeM/ewarGdRangeM now 72000 (was 48000) -- Long Distance Jamming (+50%@V, universal skill) boosts Tracking/Guidance Disruptor optimal range, 48000*1.5=72000. The 3 Tracking Disruptor magnitude fields (optical/falloff/tracking speed) and 4 Guidance Disruptor ones (missile velocity/flight time/explosion velocity/explosion radius) are boosted by TWO independent multiplicative sources confirmed live via ESI and pyfa cross-validation (2026-10-11): the Curse hull's own Amarr Cruiser skill bonus (+37.5%@V Weapon Disruption effectiveness, effect 6395) AND the universal Weapon Destabilization skill (+25%@V to the same 7 attributes, effects 3561/5793/6386, type 19767) -- these stack multiplicatively (1.375 x 1.25 = 1.71875), not just the hull bonus alone (an earlier version of this fit asserted hull-only values of -23.63625/-12.375/-16.5/+16.5, which pyfa's real numbers -29.5%/-20.6% proved incomplete -- Weapon Destabilization was the missing piece). base -17.19 * 1.71875 = -29.5453125 (tracking disruptor), base -9/-9/-12/+12 * 1.71875 = -15.46875/-15.46875/-20.625/+20.625 (guidance disruptor). ewarScramRangeM pinned at 26000 (unchanged) as a negative-path guard -- no skill or hull bonus found anywhere that touches Warp Scrambler/Disruptor strength OR a Curse's own (nonexistent) scram range bonus. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (comprehensive skill audit, P1-B): drone DPS multiplier corrected -- the RoF reduction previously applied (-20%, attributed to '[Race] Drone Specialization') was fictional, no drone RoF skill exists at all; that skill is actually a +10%@V DAMAGE bonus gated to T2 drones (reqSkill-detected), and a separate, previously entirely unmodeled weapon-size-class damage skill (+25%@V, Light/Medium/Heavy Drone Operation or Sentry Drone Interfacing, always applies) was added. Net real multiplier for a T1 drone is unchanged (1.50x1.25=1.875, same magnitude as the old 1.50/0.80 by coincidence); for a T2 drone it's 1.50x1.25x1.10=2.0625, ~10% higher than before. Separately, this fit's cached Acolyte II/Infiltrator II type snapshots were stale (missing reqSkill attributes 182/183/184 entirely, predating this file's need to read them) -- refreshed with full live ESI data 2026-10-11 as part of this same fix, which is why droneDps moved further than the formula alone would predict (138 -> 229, not just a ~10% bump) for this specific fit only. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (independent review pass, finding #2): maxActiveDrones (attribute 352) was discovered to be a CHARACTER attribute, not a ship one -- confirmed live via ESI's own attribute metadata and the absence of 352 from every checked ship's dogma_attributes -- so the old Infinity fallback was never actually a fallback at all; it was the value used on EVERY fit, unconditionally. Fixed to the correct fixed cap of 5 (MAX_ACTIVE_DRONES_SKILL_V, from the Drones skill's own description: 'Can operate 1 drone per skill level', assumed trained to V per this tool's established convention). This fit's drone bay held more than 5 combat-capable drones, so it was previously crediting more active drones than a pilot can actually control -- the corrected sandbox output (droneCount now exactly 5, greedily filled hardest-hitting-type-first, same already-audited per-drone formula) is the new expected value. Sandbox: droneCount=5 of 8 bay (3x Infiltrator II + 2x Acolyte II deployed, hardest-hitting-first), dpsFixed=droneDps=177 (unchanged: this fit has no turrets/launchers fitted, all 5 high slots are cap warfare). Note: Usually fit on Frigates and Destroyers.
438.name: 1MN Afterburner II

2404.description: Favored by many for its average capacity and firing rate. Useful in both fast attack raids and longer battles.
2404.name: Light Missile Launcher II

2410.description: Designed for long engagements between medium sized ships. Slow firing rate, but makes up for it with a large missile capacity.
2410.name: Heavy Missile Launcher II

2420.description: A massive launcher designed for extended bombardments of hard targets like battleships and stations. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
2420.name: Torpedo Launcher II

2629.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
2629.name: Scourge Fury Heavy Missile

10631.description: A tiny launcher that can carry a very limited supply of rockets. Not really intended as a primary weapon but rather as a cheap supplementary weapon system.
10631.name: Rocket Launcher II

19739.description: A battleship mounted launcher used for long range standoffs with other battleships, but less suitable for bombardment of deployed structures. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
19739.name: Cruise Missile Launcher II

20307.description: A kinetic warhead designed for use with heavy assault launchers. Heavy assault missiles can be fired at a greater rate than heavy missiles, at the expense of effective range.
20307.name: Scourge Heavy Assault Missile

24471.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

This modified version of the Scourge rocket packs a considerably stronger punch, but as a result is heavier and slower. This makes it very effective against larger targets, but markedly less effective against smaller and more agile targets.
24471.name: Scourge Rage Rocket

24477.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

A modified version of the Scourge rocket. It can reach higher velocity than the Scourge rocket at the expense of warhead size.
24477.name: Scourge Javelin Rocket

24495.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24495.name: Scourge Fury Light Missile

24501.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24501.name: Scourge Precision Light Missile

24513.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24513.name: Scourge Precision Heavy Missile

24533.description:
The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24533.name: Scourge Fury Cruise Missile

24541.description:
The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24541.name: Scourge Precision Cruise Missile

25715.description: A launcher intended for use on cruiser-class spacecraft. While assault launchers do not possess the sheer damage-dealing capability of regular heavy missile launchers, their blend of speed and attack power lends them application across a good range of tactical situations.
25715.name: Heavy Assault Missile Launcher II

Ishtar (12005) carries a hull role bonus of +25% specifically to the 'dronesentry' category (SHIP_ROLE_BONUS['12005'] = [['drone','damage',50],['dronesentry','damage',25]] -- confirmed this is a SEPARATE, smaller bonus from the 50% combat-drone bonus, and the two never stack since a given drone is either sentry or non-sentry via isSentryDrone()). Hand-derivation: Garde II explosive damage 64 (attr118) x ownMult 1.65 (attr64) x droneSkillDmgMult (MAX_DRONE_DAMAGE_MULT 1.50 x size-class-skill 1.25 x racial-spec 1.10, T2-gated-and-present = 2.0625) x Ishtar's dronesentry hull role bonus (1.25) = 272.25 dmg/cycle, / cycle time 4s (no RoF skill or role bonus applies, MAX_DRONE_ROF_MULT=1.0) = 68.0625 DPS/drone x5 drones = 340.3125, matching the sandbox-computed code output exactly (confirming the implementation, not just self-consistency).

This modified version of the Scourge rocket packs a considerably stronger punch, but as a result is heavier and slower. This makes it very effective against larger targets, but markedly less effective against smaller and more agile targets.
24471.name: Scourge Rage Rocket

24477.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

A modified version of the Scourge rocket. It can reach higher velocity than the Scourge rocket at the expense of warhead size.
24477.name: Scourge Javelin Rocket

24495.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24495.name: Scourge Fury Light Missile

24501.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24501.name: Scourge Precision Light Missile

24513.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24513.name: Scourge Precision Heavy Missile

24533.description:
The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24533.name: Scourge Fury Cruise Missile

24541.description:
The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

expected.note: CONSTRUCTED, disclosed -- see label. Hand-derived: jamStrength = 2.6(Multispectral ECM II base, all 4 types equal) * 1.25(EWAR_SKILL_ECM_STRENGTH_BONUS_PCT universal skill, independent stage) * [2x SDA II stacking-penalized: (1+0.10*1.0)*(1+0.10*0.869)=1.10*1.0869=1.19559] = 2.6*1.25*1.19559 = 3.8857 -- see actual sandbox output for exact rounding. Pre-fix (no stacking penalty between the 2 rigs) this would have shown jamStrength = 2.6*1.25*1.20 = 3.9, a small but real overstatement that grows sharply with 3 rigs (1.30 naive vs ~1.277 penalized). expected.note: Live-ESI-verified (type 484 '125mm Gatling AutoCannon I', group 55 'Projectile Weapon'; type 185 'EMP S' and 193 'EMP M', both group 83 'Projectile Ammo'): the weapon and BOTH ammo types resolve to the SAME broad category ('projectile') under weaponCategoryFromGroup()/the now-removed ammoCategoryFromGroup() -- confirmed group 83 holds every size of Projectile Ammo together, so a category-only match (the pre-fix behavior) cannot tell EMP S from EMP M. expected.note: Confirmed via the real estimateHpAndDps() run against this live-ESI data 2026-10-11: signatureRadius={base:35, boosted:79}. Pre-fix (old code, no Interceptor-group check), boosted would have been 210 -- identical to what a non-Interceptor hull with the exact same MWD shows (confirmed: a Rifter fit with this same 5MN Y-T8 MWD also gives boosted=210) -- a ~2.7x overstatement of how much an Interceptor's signature actually blooms under MWD. Mechanism: Crow's own live dogma carries attribute 568 (eliteBonusInterceptor) = -15 (confirmed, same on all 10 group-831 hulls) and effect 3766 (interceptorMWDSignatureRadiusBonus, modifies attribute 554 by 568's value) -- at assumed Interceptors@V (-15 x 5 = -75%), the MWD's own 500% sig bonus becomes 500 x 0.25 = 125%, giving boosted = 35 x 2.25 = 78.75 (rounds to 79). See INTERCEPTOR_GROUP_ID/INTERCEPTOR_MWD_SIG_BONUS_ATTR comment block in dscan-tool.html for the full live-ESI grounding (effect 3766's modifiers, cross-checked against EVE University's Crow page and pyfa's own eos/effects.py Effect6730 for where in the math this reduction has to apply).

expected.note: Live-ESI-grounded 2026-10-11 (backlog #1): Proteus hull (29988: maxVelocity 230, agility 0.56, mass 13,300,000 -- all live-ESI) + Hyperspatial Optimization (45617) fitted, nothing else. Confirmed via ESI that Proteus's 'speed+agility' Propulsion subsystem variant is GENUINELY ASYMMETRIC vs. every other race: its own in-game description says 'improves the agility AND WARP SPEED' -- agility -7.5%/lvl (attr 1520, effect subsystemBonusGallentePropulsion2Agility) -> -37.5%@V (Gallente Propulsion Systems skill@V scaling, effects 3850/4213), but it does NOT touch maxVelocity at all (0, confirmed, not an oversight) -- instead a +10%/lvl warpSpeedMultiplier bonus (attr 1440, effect subsystemBonusGallentePropulsionWarpSpeed) -> +50%@V, which this tool doesn't model anywhere (no warp-speed figure exists in the Speed/Align card) and is disclosed as a deliberately out-of-scope gap, not silently dropped. This fit pins exactly that asymmetry: speedCruising UNCHANGED from the no-bonus baseline (230*1.25=287.5, rounds to 288) while alignTimeBase reflects the real -37.5%@V agility cut (-ln(0.25)*(0.56*0.75*0.625)*13.3=4.84, rounds to 4.8). If a future change ever mistakenly gives Proteus a maxVelocity bonus (e.g. by copying another race's table entry), this fit's speedCruising assertion catches it immediately. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (backlog #16, NEGATIVE CONTROL): capacitorCapacity (1875) pinned -- this fit's Core subsystem (if any) is not one of the capacitor-bonus 'Reactor' ids, confirming SUBSYSTEM_CAPACITOR_CAPACITY_SELFADD_ATTR correctly contributes zero here. UPDATE 2026-10-13 (speed/align completeness pass): Spaceship Command V (-2%/lvl agility, every ship, pyfa evasiveManeuveringAgilityBonusPostPercentAgilityShip on skill 3327) was never modeled -- every align time x0.90.  New values: alignTimeBase 4.4.

29990.description: For many Minmatar, the high mountains of Matar hold wonders unknown to the rest of New Eden: hidden glens, beautiful creatures, buried customs. Not surprisingly, the Krusual tribe lay claim to these mountains, their home for generations and base to their machinations. Krusual elders whisper ancient tales among their huddled tribes, describing the glory of heroes past and enigmatic prophecies of old. On the darkest day, at the most hopeless moments, an elder may speak of Loki, in reverent tones and excited hushes. In the ancient tongue, the Loki are the crux of Krusual thought. There is no direct translation for this word; in fact, Loki translates differently among the elders. It can mean “hidden wonder” or “secret passage”, “changing mask” or “unseen dagger”. Regardless of its context, Loki has one meaning common to all its tales across all the elders: “hope”.

47918.description:
This medium-sized Entropic Disintegrator is normally seen in use on Triglavian cruisers or battlecruisers, which are able to handle the increased radiation and serious gravitational tidal forces the weapon generates as a side-effect of its operation.

Entropic Disintegrators draw on the tremendous power of the Triglavian singularity-based energy systems to convert exotic matter into a particle stream directed with locally generated entropic force. While powerful, the range of the weapon is limited by the attenuation of entropic forces, which dissipate critically beyond the optimal range. As a result this weapon has no falloff range.

The particle stream generates thermal and explosive reactions on impact, and the entropic forces resolve into a localized gravitational conduit that steadily increases the acceleration on the exotic particles. In effect, the weapon's damage potential increases to a maximum level as long as the particle stream is kept on the same target.

Requires either standard or advanced exotic plasma charge ammo types: Baryon, Meson, Tetryon, Mystic, and Occult.
47918.name: Heavy Entropic Disintegrator II

47929.description:
An Entropic Disintegrator uses charges of exotic plasma to provide the particle feedstock for the weapon's beam, with different forms of exotic matter modulating the beam's characteristics.

Meson Exotic Plasma charges yield a beam with a very long range but reduced thermal and explosive damage potential.
47929.name: Meson Exotic Plasma M

expected.note: Missile damage-application-efficiency feature (missile-side only, 2026-10-11 -- user direction: 'ship missile-side only for now... keep turret-side in the backlog'). Hand-derived via the eveuniversity.org-sourced formula appliedFraction=min(1, S/E, ((S/E)*(Ve/Vt))^drf): bare Rifter sig radius S=35 (hull attr552, live-ESI, no rigs/sig-bloom modules fitted), cruising speed Vt=456.25 (hull attr37=365 x the file's own MAX_NAVIGATION_MULT=1.25-at-V convention, no prop mod fitted so this IS the only speed state). Reference ammo (live-ESI, MISSILE_CLASS_REFERENCE_AMMO): Rocket Ve=150/E=20/drf=0.644 -> 70.0%; Light Missile Ve=170/E=40/drf=0.604 -> 50.8%; Heavy Missile Ve=85/E=140/drf=0.682 -> 12.4%; HAM Ve=101/E=125/drf=0.882 -> 8.6%; Cruise Ve=69/E=330/drf=0.882 -> 2.6%; Torpedo Ve=78/E=405/drf=0.944 -> 1.9%. All 6 hand-computed values matched the sandboxed estimateHpAndDps() output EXACTLY (not just the pinned top-ranked Rocket here) -- confirms the formula, the per-class reference-ammo live fetch, and the ranking/sort are all wired correctly end-to-end. Rocket correctly ranks #1 (small, fast missile vs. a tiny frigate-class signature) -- the intuitively-correct answer, cross-checked against this exact kind of guidance already given informally on eveuniversity.org's own Missile_mechanics examples. T2 TIERS + APPLIED-DPS METRIC CORRECTION ADDED 2026-10-12 (the owner's own fix: ranking by application % alone conflates 'lands more often' with 'deals more damage' -- see MISSILE_REC_METRIC in dscan-tool.html). Field renamed missileBestClass*->missileBest* (now carries the tier too, e.g. 'Precision Light Missile'). On this fit, Rocket (T1) is STILL the #1 pick under the new appliedDps metric (confirmed via sandbox, not assumed) -- Confirmed via a revert-sanity-check (MISSILE_REC_METRIC forced back to applicationPct in a throwaway copy) that this assertion DOES actually flip under the old metric too -- Precision Light Missile wins instead of Rocket (76.9%/70.1% application vs. Rocket's 70%/63%) -- so this fit also exercises the metric switch, not just the Megathron fit below. UPDATE 2026-10-16 (v2026.10.14.27, hand-tables P5): your missiles now get the All V application skills (Guided Missile Precision -25% explosion radius, Target Navigation Prediction +50% explosion velocity; pyfa Effect1472 / 1590), so the best pick and its numbers moved: was {'missileBestCruising': 'Rocket', 'missileBestCruisingPct': 70, 'missileBestCruisingAppliedDps': 5.78}. Expected values from tools/independent_checks/check_missile_application.py (SDE ammo values, EVE's application formula), e.g. Megathron: Scourge Torpedo E 405 x 0.75 = 303.75 m, Ve 78 x 1.5 = 117 m/s vs sig 380 / 152.5 m/s: min(1, 1.251, (1.251 x 117 / 152.5)^0.944) = 96.2%.

expected.note: Confirmed via the real estimateHpAndDps() run against this live-ESI data 2026-10-11: signatureRadius={base:35, boosted:79}. Pre-fix (old code, no Interceptor-group check), boosted would have been 210 -- identical to what a non-Interceptor hull with the exact same MWD shows (confirmed: a Rifter fit with this same 5MN Y-T8 MWD also gives boosted=210) -- a ~2.7x overstatement of how much an Interceptor's signature actually blooms under MWD. Mechanism: Crow's own live dogma carries attribute 568 (eliteBonusInterceptor) = -15 (confirmed, same on all 10 group-831 hulls) and effect 3766 (interceptorMWDSignatureRadiusBonus, modifies attribute 554 by 568's value) -- at assumed Interceptors@V (-15 x 5 = -75%), the MWD's own 500% sig bonus becomes 500 x 0.25 = 125%, giving boosted = 35 x 2.25 = 78.75 (rounds to 79). See INTERCEPTOR_GROUP_ID/INTERCEPTOR_MWD_SIG_BONUS_ATTR comment block in dscan-tool.html for the full live-ESI grounding (effect 3766's modifiers, cross-checked against EVE University's Crow page and pyfa's own eos/effects.py Effect6730 for where in the math this reduction has to apply). MISSILE APPLICATION ASSERTIONS ADDED 2026-10-11 (missile damage-application-efficiency feature, missile-side only per user direction): cruising state (sig=35, speed=538 -- unboosted, MWD off) ranks Rocket best at 63.0%; boosted state (sig=79, speed=3790 -- MWD on, both numbers already independently verified by this fit's own pre-existing signatureRadiusBase/Boosted assertions) ranks Rocket best at 30.2% -- application drops sharply once the MWD both blooms the Crow's own signature AND multiplies its speed by ~7x, confirming the dual-state pairing never cross-mixes base-sig with boosted-speed or vice versa (which would produce very different, physically-nonsensical numbers). Hand-derived boosted Rocket fraction (sig=79, speed=3790 from this fit's own rounded display values) gives 30.3%, 0.1pp off the sandbox's 30.2% -- expected and consistent with this project's established rounding-on-unrounded-intermediates convention (see e.g. draugur/kikimora rangeOptimalM notes elsewhere in this file): the sandbox computes missileAppliedFraction() off the UNROUNDED internal sig/speed values, not the already-rounded 79/3790 shown in the UI. Rocket stays #1 in both states here (small/fast ammo vs. a small Interceptor hull in both states), unlike a case where boosting speed enough could flip the ranking to a slower-but-tighter-explosion-radius class -- that flip case is NOT separately covered by a golden fit this session (noted as a disclosed gap, not a silent omission). T2 TIERS + APPLIED-DPS METRIC CORRECTION ADDED 2026-10-12 (the owner's own fix: ranking by application % alone conflates 'lands more often' with 'deals more damage' -- see MISSILE_REC_METRIC in dscan-tool.html). Field renamed missileBestClass*->missileBest* (now carries the tier too, e.g. 'Precision Light Missile'). On this fit, Rocket (T1) is STILL the #1 pick under the new appliedDps metric (confirmed via sandbox, not assumed) -- Confirmed via a revert-sanity-check (MISSILE_REC_METRIC forced back to applicationPct in a throwaway copy) that this assertion DOES actually flip under the old metric too -- Precision Light Missile wins instead of Rocket (76.9%/70.1% application vs. Rocket's 70%/63%) -- so this fit also exercises the metric switch, not just the Megathron fit below. UPDATE 2026-10-16 (v2026.10.14.27, hand-tables P5): your missiles now get the All V application skills (Guided Missile Precision -25% explosion radius, Target Navigation Prediction +50% explosion velocity; pyfa Effect1472 / 1590), so the best pick and its numbers moved: was {'missileBestCruising': 'Rocket', 'missileBestCruisingPct': 63, 'missileBestCruisingAppliedDps': 5.2, 'missileBestBoosted': 'Rocket', 'missileBestBoostedPct': 30.2, 'missileBestBoostedAppliedDps': 2.49}. Expected values from tools/independent_checks/check_missile_application.py (SDE ammo values, EVE's application formula), e.g. Megathron: Scourge Torpedo E 405 x 0.75 = 303.75 m, Ve 78 x 1.5 = 117 m/s vs sig 380 / 152.5 m/s: min(1, 1.251, (1.251 x 117 / 152.5)^0.944) = 96.2%.

A deliberately modified clone of the real curse_zkb139073592_ewar killmail (zKillboard 139073592) with its one flag-19 (module-paired) Navy Cap Booster 800 charge item removed, leaving only the 4 spare ones that were already sitting in Cargo (flag 5) in the real data -- same real ESI type/group stubs, same ship, same every other module, so dpsFixed/totalHP/etc. are identical to the unmodified Curse fit (this change touches nothing but one mid-slot charge item). This modified version of the Scourge rocket packs a considerably stronger punch, but as a result is heavier and slower. This makes it very effective against larger targets, but markedly less effective against smaller and more agile targets.

24477.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

A modified version of the Scourge rocket. It can reach higher velocity than the Scourge rocket at the expense of warhead size.

24495.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24495.name: Scourge Fury Light Missile

24501.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24501.name: Scourge Precision Light Missile

24513.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.

24533.description:

expected.note: Hand-verified against Shield Power Relay II's real dogma attributes (attr144=1.35, confirmed via the local pyfa SDE cache -- no attr147, so capacity is untouched): capacity = 250*1.25 = 312.5 -> 313 (same as the bare-hull baseline). rechargeTimeSec = 125000*0.75*1.35/1000 = 126.5625s (SLOWER than the bare-hull 93.75s -- a real penalty, the opposite direction from every other module in CAPACITOR_RECHARGE_MULT_GROUPS); peakRechargeRate = 2.5*312.5/126.5625 = 6.17 -> 6.2 (down from the bare-hull baseline's 8.3), confirming the KNOWN OPEN ITEM #1 fix's new capRechargeTimePenaltyFractions pool correctly SLOWS recharge rather than being miscombined with the existing reduction pool as a bonus. 2026-10-12 EXTENDED: also carries attr338=-25 (rechargeratebonus), the module's real shield-side bonus -- see SHIELD_POWER_RELAY_RECHARGE_ATTR's comment in index.html. rawShieldHP stays at the baseline's 563 (attr338 never touches capacity) while shieldRechargeTimeSec = 468.75*0.75 = 351.5625s -> peak = 2.5*562.5/351.5625 = 4.0 exactly, up from baseline's 3 -- isolating that this module's own cap-recharge PENALTY (attr144, above) and its shield-recharge BONUS (attr338) are read from two completely different real attributes and never miscombined into the same pool.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24501.name: Scourge Precision Light Missile

210.description: From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.
210.name: Scourge Light Missile

19739.description: A battleship mounted launcher used for long range standoffs with other battleships, but less suitable for bombardment of deployed structures. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
19739.name: Cruise Missile Launcher II

2629.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
2629.name: Scourge Fury Heavy Missile

2404.description: Favored by many for its average capacity and firing rate. Useful in both fast attack raids and longer battles.
2404.name: Light Missile Launcher II

24533.description:
The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24533.name: Scourge Fury Cruise Missile

expected.note: 'start on 1 and 2 together' -- effect-audit leftovers on the EWAR / Misc card): Scorpion + Burst Jammer II + Multispectral ECM II + Large Particle Dispersion Projector II rig. The ECM Burst's radius ecmBurstRange gets Long Distance Jamming V (+50%), the rig's +25% (pyfa Effect2491, unpenalized) and the Scorpion's ECM Burst range bonus (Effect2812); the rig's +25% ECM range (Effect1452, penalized) was already modelled and is pinned here for the first time. 203.description: The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.
203.name: Scourge Cruise Missile

20307.description: A kinetic warhead designed for use with heavy assault launchers. Heavy assault missiles can be fired at a greater rate than heavy missiles, at the expense of effective range.
20307.name: Scourge Heavy Assault Missile

24541.description:
The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24541.name: Scourge Precision Cruise Missile

10631.description: A tiny launcher that can carry a very limited supply of rockets. Not really intended as a primary weapon but rather as a cheap supplementary weapon system.
10631.name: Rocket Launcher II

24513.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24513.name: Scourge Precision Heavy Missile

24495.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24495.name: Scourge Fury Light Missile

24477.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

A modified version of the Scourge rocket. It can reach higher velocity than the Scourge rocket at the expense of warhead size.
24477.name: Scourge Javelin Rocket

267.description: An ultra-heavy piercing missile. While it is a slow projectile, its sheer damage potential is simply staggering.
267.name: Scourge Torpedo

2420.description: A massive launcher designed for extended bombardments of hard targets like battleships and stations. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
2420.name: Torpedo Launcher II

2410.description: Designed for long engagements between medium sized ships. Slow firing rate, but makes up for it with a large missile capacity.
2410.name: Heavy Missile Launcher II

25715.description: A launcher intended for use on cruiser-class spacecraft. While assault launchers do not possess the sheer damage-dealing capability of regular heavy missile launchers, their blend of speed and attack power lends them application across a good range of tactical situations.

The first Minmatar-made large missile. Constructed of reactionary alloys, the Scourge cruise missile is built to get to the target. Guidance and propulsion systems are of Gallente origin and were initially used in drones, making this a nimble projectile despite its heavy payload.

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24533.name: Scourge Fury Cruise Missile
